linkedin.hook: Why pooled liquidity models fail institutional debt strategies on Stellar Soroban.
linkedin.copy:
Most lending infrastructure forces capital into shared risk pools, socializing default parameters across unrelated positions. When wrapping yield-bearing assets like Blend v2 b-tokens, this design introduces systemic exposure that risk desks refuse to underwrite. The alternative requires isolating state execution at the sub-account level without fracturing shared on-chain liquidity.

Vanna handles this through isolated SmartAccounts running directly on Soroban. By ingesting formally verified Blend v2 b-token specifications as core collateral, we allow balance-sheet isolation where recursive borrowing terminates at a strict 1.10x Health Factor floor. Risk parameters apply strictly to the individual contract sandbox rather than the aggregate market.

Execution performance dictates whether automated deleveraging succeeds under stress. With ~320ms Mercury indexer latency reading state changes and base operations costing 0.00014 XLM in fixed network gas, debt positions can be rebalanced in sub-second windows without slippage bleed. Institutional testnet access is open at test.stellar.vanna.finance.

Institutional architecture is documented at test.stellar.vanna.finance

reddit.hook: Deep dive: Ingesting Blend v2 b-tokens into Vanna SmartAccounts for leveraged loops on Soroban
reddit.copy:
We just pushed our testnet implementation for looping Blend v2 b-tokens, and I want to break down the mechanics behind how Vanna SmartAccounts handle the debt accounting without blowing past Soroban resource limits.

### Architecture and b-token Ingestion
Blend v2 relies on b-tokens as interest-bearing receipt tokens for pooled supply positions. Instead of holding these passively, our SmartAccount architecture wraps the b-token contract balance and locks it into an isolated state machine. The user never holds the raw debt on their master key; the SmartAccount acts as the proxy borrower.

Because Blend pools rely on variable utilization curves, recursive leverage usually blows out gas budgets on older EVM rollups. On Soroban, invocation costs sit at roughly 0.00014 XLM. This allows an account to supply USDC, receive bUSDC, borrow XLM against it, swap back to USDC, and re-supply within a single batch invocation without incurring rent spikes.

### Risk Parameters and Telemetry
We enforce a rigid 1.10x Health Factor floor inside the verification layer. Liquidations do not touch the global pool reserves; they unwind directly inside the user SmartAccount sandbox by burning the underlying b-tokens against the debt principal.

Telemetry is handled via a dedicated Mercury indexer instance running at ~320ms read latency. This ensures liquidator bots and margin calls pick up balance shifts before oracle deviations cause bad debt accumulation.

### Testing the Sandbox
You can run this loop yourself right now. Head over to test.stellar.vanna.finance and spin up an account sandbox using testnet funds. Mint mock collateral, open a credit line against the Blend v2 test pool, and check the health factor telemetry under recursive calls.

Disclosure: I am a core engineer building Vanna Protocol. Testnet contracts are currently under audit and parameters are subject to tuning based on liquidation stress tests.
